name: Chicken Breast (Cooked, Boneless)
notes: Excellent lean protein source. Always serve plain — no seasoning, garlic, or onion.

name: Salmon (Cooked)
notes: Rich in omega-3 fatty acids. Must be fully cooked — raw salmon can carry fatal parasites.

name: Turkey (Cooked, Plain)
notes: Lean, digestible protein. Remove skin and bones. No seasoning.

name: Beef (Lean, Cooked)
notes: Good protein and iron source. Choose lean cuts; high fat can cause pancreatitis.

name: Eggs (Cooked)
notes: Complete protein. Scrambled, boiled, or poached — no butter or salt.

name: Cottage Cheese (Low Fat)
notes: Lower lactose than other dairy. Good for bland diet. Small amounts only.

name: White Rice (Cooked)
notes: Classic bland diet staple. Easily digestible — ideal for upset stomachs.

name: Oatmeal (Plain, Cooked)
notes: Good soluble fiber. Plain only — no sugar, raisins, or flavoring.

name: Sweet Potato (Cooked)
notes: Excellent source of vitamins A, C, and fiber. Plain, no seasonings or butter.

name: Carrots (Raw or Cooked)
notes: Low calorie, high fiber. Great for teeth. A dog's favorite crunchy snack.

name: Green Beans (Plain)
notes: Low calorie. Good for weight management — can replace up to 10% of kibble.

name: Cucumber
notes: Very low calorie and hydrating. Great summer treat.

name: Pumpkin (Plain Puree)
notes: Excellent for GI health. Helps with both diarrhea and constipation. Not pie filling.

name: Peas
notes: Safe as a treat. Avoid canned (high sodium). Some debate about grain-free diets with peas as primary ingredient.

name: Blueberries
notes: Antioxidant powerhouse. Great training treat. High water content.

name: Watermelon (Seedless, No Rind)
notes: Hydrating. Remove seeds and rind. Good summer treat.

name: Apple (Flesh, No Seeds/Core)
notes: Good source of fiber and vitamins. Remove core and seeds — seeds contain amygdalin.

name: Banana
notes: Safe in small amounts. High in sugar — limit for overweight or diabetic dogs.

name: Strawberries
notes: Safe and enjoyed by most dogs. High in vitamin C. Limit for diabetic dogs.

name: Mango (Pitted, No Skin)
notes: Safe without pit or skin. High in vitamins A, C, E, and B6.

name: Peanut Butter (Xylitol-Free)
notes: ALWAYS check label for xylitol — it is deadly. Natural, unsalted varieties preferred. High calorie — use sparingly.

name: Plain Popcorn (Air-Popped)
notes: Plain only. Avoid kernels — choking hazard. No butter, salt, or flavoring.

name: Bread (Plain White)
notes: Not toxic in small amounts but no nutritional value. Avoid bread with raisins, garlic, or xylitol.

name: Broccoli
notes: Safe in very small amounts (under 10% of diet). Large amounts cause significant GI upset due to isothiocyanates.

name: Spinach
notes: Contains oxalic acid which can affect kidney function in large quantities. Avoid in dogs with kidney disease.

name: Coconut Flesh
notes: Not toxic but high in fat. Small amounts are fine. Coconut water is high in potassium — avoid.

name: Dairy / Cheese
notes: Many dogs are lactose intolerant. Hard cheese in tiny amounts is usually tolerated. Avoid soft cheeses, large amounts of milk, or ice cream.

name: Peaches (Flesh Only, No Pit)
notes: Remove pit and stem completely. Flesh in small amounts is safe — pit contains amygdalin (cyanide precursor).

name: Cinnamon
notes: Small amounts in food are unlikely to harm but can irritate mouth and digestive tract. Cinnamon oil is concentrated — avoid.

name: Raw Meat
notes: Carries bacterial risk (Salmonella, Listeria) for both dogs and humans. If feeding raw, use commercially prepared, pathogen-tested products.

name: Chocolate
notes: TOXIC. Theobromine and caffeine cause life-threatening toxicity. Dark and baking chocolate most dangerous. Emergency vet immediately.

name: Grapes & Raisins
notes: TOXIC. Can cause sudden kidney failure. No safe dose known. Emergency vet immediately.

name: Onions & Garlic
notes: TOXIC. All alliums (onion, garlic, leek, chive) destroy red blood cells causing hemolytic anemia. Cooked, powdered, and raw all equally dangerous.

name: Macadamia Nuts
notes: TOXIC. Causes weakness, vomiting, hyperthermia, and tremors. Call vet immediately.

name: Avocado
notes: TOXIC. Persin in flesh, skin, and leaves is toxic. Pit is a deadly obstruction hazard.

name: Xylitol Products (Sugar-Free)
notes: DEADLY. Causes rapid insulin release and liver failure. Found in gum, candy, some peanut butters, baked goods. Always check labels.

name: Corn Cob
notes: The cob (not kernels) causes life-threatening intestinal obstruction. Emergency surgery often required. Never give dogs access to corn cobs.

name: Wild Mushrooms
notes: POTENTIALLY FATAL. Amanita species (death cap, destroying angel) can kill with no antidote. Never allow dogs near wild mushrooms.

name: Raw Yeast Dough
notes: TOXIC. Expands in stomach (can rupture) and produces ethanol. Emergency vet required.

name: Nutmeg
notes: TOXIC. Contains myristicin causing tremors, seizures, and disorientation.

name: Dry Dog Kibble (Standard)
notes: Primary food source. Caloric density varies by brand — check packaging for kcal/cup.

name: Wet/Canned Dog Food
notes: Higher moisture content (~78%). Lower calorie density than kibble. Check label for kcal/can.

name: Raw Dog Food (Commercial)
notes: Safe when commercially prepared and handled properly. Pathogen-tested products recommended.

name: Dog Treats (Standard)
notes: Treats should not exceed 10% of daily caloric intake. Check label for kcal per treat.

name: Dental Chews
notes: Count calories toward daily intake. Choose VOHC-approved products for proven dental benefit.

name: Raspberries
notes: Safe in very small amounts. Contains trace amounts of xylitol naturally — only a concern in very large quantities. Good antioxidants.

name: Tomatoes (Ripe Red)
notes: Ripe red tomato flesh in small amounts is generally safe. Green parts (leaves, stems, unripe) contain solanine — avoid.

name: Honey
notes: Safe for healthy adult dogs in tiny amounts. Avoid for puppies under 1 year (botulism risk) and diabetic dogs.

name: Lentils
notes: Cooked lentils are safe in moderate amounts. Good fiber source. Some concern about legume-heavy grain-free diets — discuss with vet.

name: Quinoa (Cooked)
notes: Safe and nutritious. Some dogs may have digestive sensitivity — introduce gradually.
